title: Verify repeat-visit boundary transfers before extending cache lifetime
problem: Current public staging already reuses all three Mozambique boundary files on a warm page load and returns 304 for forced conditional GETs. Historical 30–50% repeat-transfer savings remain unverified; a specific unmet cache/latency/freshness scenario is needed before an optimization.
humanitarian_relevance: Reducing repeated loading cost may help users of a humanitarian risk-monitoring tool on constrained networks. No measured operational or beneficiary outcome.

evidence.claim: Issue author estimated 30–50% savings on an older preview by versioning heavy JSON assets. Not independently reproduced or assumed current.

September 9 staging boundary HEAD returns JSON, Content-Length 17,207,428 and max-age=3600; conditional HEAD returns 304. The production-named host returns 642-byte HTML at that path. These checks download no boundary body and measure neither GET transfer nor browser cache behavior.
Pinned code uses stable public JSON paths and already caches boundary data/promises in memory by layer/ISO3. Existing tests mock the loader. Entry point unregisters the service worker.

Eleven controlled cases executing the unchanged pinned request wrapper in Canary pass, including expired unchanged/changed responses and freshness controls. Live staging loads 4,485,559 compressed body bytes initially, then zero reported boundary transfer on a warm load. Three forced conditional GETs return 304, with 768 total CDP encoded response bytes. Natural live one-hour expiry and user revisit patterns are not measured.

code_surface: At master 603710958a025f15507164ccdaa24bc2515b70dc: frontend/vite.config.ts, firebase.json, scripts/country_build.sh, config/mozambique/layers.json, context/layers/boundary.ts, utils/boundary-cache.ts and its tests; fetchWithTimeout wrapper inspected and executed with original body and browser-native fetch.
proposed_change: Do not implement a cache change from the historical percentage alone. Ask for a concrete retransferring or latency-sensitive scenario; if justified and accepted, scope versioned assets while preserving update discovery and rollback behavior.
tests: Eleven controlled original-wrapper browser cases pass with independent server logs. Two live observation runs confirm cold/warm behavior; the second adds three forced conditional GETs, all 304. Canary 155.0.8046.0. No complete frontend Jest/build baseline or other-browser matrix.
environment: Existing Node 24.19.0 and bundled Playwright 1.62.1; fresh automated Canary contexts. Synthetic loopback server and real public staging observation require no accounts or deployment. Wrapper source hash verified; only reviewed imports replaced by fail-fast sentinels and TypeScript syntax erased. Lockfile registry inventory completed, full transitive/lifecycle audit not. No target install or full frontend build.
maintainer: Measured cache results and a narrow question were delivered as humanifest-bot at 2026-09-09T10:06:07Z. Await a specific unmet scenario and confirmation of bot participation; no accepted implementation scope. Manual September 15 review while other queue research continues.
risks: Measured cases already avoid repeat payloads. Historical savings, natural live one-hour expiry, eviction/restarts, other browsers and operational latency remain unverified. Synthetic two-second expiry is distinct from live forced validation. Extending freshness on mutable paths can hide changed data.
priority_rationale: Verification provides disconfirming evidence against unconditional large repeat-transfer savings. Await a specific useful scenario before spending implementation compute, and continue independent queue research.
